FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.98
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: FIND — evaluate_fix() claims sandboxed fix evaluation, but test execution is not actually wired to the patched source tree. In bench/endocrine.py, evaluate_fix() writes only the target file into a temp dir and then runs test_cmd unchanged with cwd=tmpdir. The default caller in immune_agents.py passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", "-x", "-q", "--tb=no", "--no-header", "-q"]`. From the temp dir, that command points at the original repo tests or fails to locate them, while imports resolve against the original source tree because the rest of the package was never copied. This means tests do not exercise the patched module in isolation, violating the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” behavior.
FOLLOW: Downstream, SAFE/HARMFUL verdicts can be silently wrong. A fix that breaks package-level imports, neighboring modules, or integration behavior can still be marked SAFE because only single-file static counts changed and tests either run against original code or fail for path reasons unrelated to the patch. immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline() uses SAFE/NEUTRAL to set `finding.verified = True`; verified findings then activate the NK bug-closed gate and suppress future reports. So a falsely SAFE verdict can prematurely close a live bug and mislead insect_brain relay summaries into presenting it as CLOSED.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when evaluating a fix, copy the full relevant source tree into the temp dir (at minimum the `bench/` package and tests), write the patched file at its original relative path inside that copy, and run tests against that temp tree using the temp tree as cwd/PYTHONPATH. Do not run unchanged repo-relative test commands against a temp dir containing only one file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — scan_health() misreports missing tools as available. In bench/endocrine.py, each runner returns `[]` when `_run_tool()` reports `stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`, and scan_health() then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` unconditionally unless an exception was raised. Evidence: run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy all convert NOT_FOUND into empty diagnostics instead of surfacing unavailability, and scan_health has no other availability check.
FOLLOW: This creates a fail-open health scan: the endocrine layer can report a clean scan with zero diagnostics while all analyzers are absent. insect_brain consumes health_scan as a structured health signal for round decisions; zero diagnostics from “available” tools is materially different from “tool unavailable”. It also corrupts reviewer-facing telemetry and can hide infrastructure regressions in the PoC happy path, since the whole health monitor appears to function while doing nothing.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — propagate tool availability explicitly from each runner or from _run_tool returncode/stderr, and in scan_health mark a tool unavailable when invocation returned NOT_FOUND or TIMEOUT instead of treating empty diagnostics as success.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56
DESCRIPTION: FIND — evaluate_fix() computes HARMFUL/SAFE from net total issue count, allowing cross-tool cancellation to hide newly introduced defects. In _compute_fix_verdict(), `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`; only `total_net > 0` is HARMFUL. A fix that removes two ruff warnings but introduces one new bandit issue yields total_net = -1 and is marked SAFE, despite adding a security defect.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix verification can bless fixes that regress correctness or security as long as another tool’s counts improve more. Because immune_agents marks SAFE or NEUTRAL fixes as verified, a fix that introduces a real new defect can still close the finding and stop further rounds from revisiting it. This is silently wrong output, not just noisy scoring.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify a fix as HARMFUL if any individual net count is positive (`net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`); only consider SAFE when no category worsened and at least one improved or tests passed.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the target-file resolver can patch the wrong source file when filenames overlap. In _find_target_file(), a match is accepted if `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. The substring branch is unsafe: a short mention like `brain.py` or a partial path can match unrelated paths containing that fragment, and if multiple source_paths share a basename or suffix-like fragment the first one wins arbitrarily.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix evaluation may patch and analyze the wrong file while still returning a concrete verdict for the finding_id. That produces false SAFE/HARMFUL judgments detached from the actual finding. Since the result is keyed only by finding_id, later stages cannot detect the mismatch and may mark the wrong bug as verified.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require exact basename match first, then exact normalized relative-path suffix match; if multiple source_paths match, return UNEVALUABLE instead of picking the first substring hit.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: FIND — health_trend() produces ragged time series that omit zero-count rounds for categories absent in a scan. It appends counts only for categories present in each scan’s `counts_by_category`; categories missing in a round get no entry. After scans like `{security: 1}` then `{style: 1}`, the returned trend is `{"security": [1], "style": [1]}` instead of aligned per-round series like `{"security": [1,0], "style": [0,1]}`.
FOLLOW: Any consumer comparing category trends across rounds receives malformed history and can misread disappearance as missing data rather than zero. Since this method exists specifically “for the insect brain to detect worsening/improving code health,” ragged vectors make trend analysis and thresholding unreliable.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — build the union of categories across scan history and emit one count per round per category, inserting 0 when a category is absent in a given scan.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the advertised defect-detection capability is partially dead code. endocrine.py declares DefectCategory.OFF_BY_ONE and RACE_CONDITION, and the module docstring claims defect classification for “off-by-one” and “race conditions,” but no categoriser path in run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy ever emits either category. All pyright/mypy diagnostics collapse to TYPE_SAFETY or NULL_DEREF; ruff mostly maps to DEAD_CODE/STYLE/SECURITY.
FOLLOW: Downstream, counts_by_category and any reviewer relying on endocrine defect categories will never see those categories fire, so the feature does not deliver the claimed coverage. In a PoC this is medium severity rather than critical, but it is still misleading telemetry and effectively dead functionality.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — either add minimal pattern-based mappings that can actually emit OFF_BY_ONE and RACE_CONDITION from tool messages, or remove those categories from the advertised capability until supported. The simpler sufficient fix is to stop advertising unsupported categories.
VERIFIED: TRUE
